summary: API-GW slow-read surge triggering upstream crash chain and elevated 5xx rate for AcmeCorp
description:
Issue summary: During a planned tenant capacity shift for AcmeCorp in us-west we observed a sustained slow-read pattern from a subset of client keepalive connections. The slow-read pattern caused backlog in the API gateway accept/dispatch path which amplified into upstream runtime evictions and GPU ephemeral OOMs, producing a cascade of 5xx responses across both streaming and short-request routes.

Impact: ~15% elevated 5xx rate for AcmeCorp traffic in us-west over a 30-minute window (2026-03-13 15:20-15:50 UTC). Several customer sessions experienced streaming disconnects and increased tail latency. Billing-sensitive batch embedding jobs were retried by clients, increasing load.

Immediate mitigation: We temporarily disabled a permissive keepalive policy for AcmeCorp routes at the edge and enabled aggressive conn close on slow-read >60s. That reduced accept-queue growth and stabilized new request success rates while SRE continued investigation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate long-lived connections with very slow read rates (read interval >30s) against a streaming route behind API-GW in us-west.
2) Ramp other small requests to the same tenant namespace to trigger accept queue growth.
3) Observe accept queue length at API-GW and corresponding runtime proxy queue depth.
4) Watch for runtime worker preemption logs and GPU OOM/error counters.
5) Reproduce locally with an isolated copy of the serving-runtime with slow client behavior to confirm same crash pattern.
comments: Support (Jamie): Initial customer report received at 2026-03-13T15:27Z — AcmeCorp reported streaming disconnects and retries leading to elevated error counts in their telemetry.

SRE (Arun): Collected API-GW accept queue and proxy metrics; observed slow-read clients holding connections open and pushing keepalive bytes at >30s intervals. Increased accept queue correlated with runtime worker preemptions.
Customer (AcmeCorp - Maya): Confirmed we deployed a new webhook connector that held long polling sockets; rolling it back reduced but did not eliminate the errors.

SRE (Arun): Applied temporary edge policy to aggressively close slow-read sessions and disabled keepalive reuse for affected routes — new request success rate improved within 3 minutes. Continuing root cause analysis on runtime eviction behavior.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Slow-read clients cause API-GW accept/disptach backlog which starves runtime proxy threadpools and triggers worker eviction cascade.
Hypothesis 2: Evicted workers leave behind partial KV cache handles leading to increased memory fragmentation and sporadic GPU OOMs under mixed embed/chat load.

Finding: Timeline correlation shows accept-queue spike precedes runtime eviction logs by ~90s and NVML OOMs by ~120s. Eviction logs reference prefetch_lock_wait patterns consistent with kvcache contention.
Trace snippets: Linked traces show hedged retries from client side coinciding with apigw retry amplification; retry policy caused bursts of short requests while streaming sockets remained half-open.

Related artifacts: Slack #support thread link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1678800000000, dashboard: /dashboards/tenant-acmecorp-us-west-acceptqueue, suspect PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4372 (prior prefetch change)
Note: Similar but not identical patterns observed in SUP-472901 and SUP-720304 (referenced for remediation ideas) — not a direct duplicate.
resolution:
Workaround applied: edge keepalive/slow-read policy tightened for affected tenant routes and aggressive conn close enabled. AcmeCorp rolled back the webhook connector causing long polling behavior which stopped the initial driver. SRE implemented a short-term runtime config change to reduce prefetch lock hold times and added more conservative hedged retry throttles at the gateway to avoid amplification.

Follow-ups: 1) Engineering will land a fix to add accept-queue backpressure signals from API-GW to the scheduler to avoid worker preemption cascades (tracked in github PR 4372). 2) Product/Docs to publish guidance for customers on safe long-poll patterns and keepalive settings. 3) Post-incident: create a dashboard alert for accept-queue growth + runtime eviction correlation and run a canary test for the prefetch config change.

Status: Mitigation validated and error rates returned to baseline for AcmeCorp in us-west. Follow-up items assigned to SRE and Runtime teams.
